title: How Unions Pave the Way to the American Dream
author: Roxanne D. Brown
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/07/Cincinnati_Union_Terminal_Ceiling-680x453.jpg)

Photograph Source: Arun Sreeranganathan - [CC BY
4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)

Marcelo Assis recalled how his family arrived in the United States about 35
years ago, “poor as hell”—yet certain that America offered the path forward
that they’d never find in their native Brazil or anywhere else.

The following years brought ups and downs, with Marcelo serving as a combat
medic in the Army and then falling disillusioned with low-paying nonunion work
that held him back instead of helping him move ahead.

But Marcelo ultimately landed back-to-back union jobs that catapulted him into
the middle class and firmly anchored him there. Just as he clearly recalls his
arrival in this country, Marcelo vividly remembers the moment years later when
he looked around his newly purchased home, thought about the good life he
provided to his family, and realized for the first time that he’d made it.

“This is the American dream,” he said to himself.

Marcelo’s experience shows how unions pave the way to a brighter future.
That’s true even now—a time when the majority of working people feel as though
the American dream has slipped out of reach because of [rampant economic
inequality](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BD6F5yqG0GtuZHtrN4C0Ywxb2CnP04MgKno5xX5Sau53Uw9j5lhNnToM8NzeEj5MLdEP9qKFKngnyz1YBT7mDas-3DZOn9_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Btfc4jeVCORt8ioA1M5PxwjGrtjF6IXFwVnowFH8MFIxJx-2Bz2FT4p75MittqFQqF4xToieODwbyqLb-2BSob5ztnoFqMsaNloKNKn4m54N2x7ZetfjDBEv7m9xHbs7wvEmhHiTZeL-2FS108x-2FKkP4d-2FiMo-2FY5Fo-2FpAF-2BNwNv6aTupu04Y34RgDHHcO88Vdzqc9rfr3cq3ZrgPCCuXCEBEzUS-2BOGMugzBxutgOkIxuPN-2BZ88qL1OLkevgz7HxUNlXwL8dHIJzkOA8g9fvK-2Bcy3Z-2FMu57-2FN-2ByvjrAXhFB6fL3iQ0Cw-2Bm6211A-2FUKOlEbkWTzEpQ8pfUYvZ-2F2CEPIiz3VASBMSpfy6QNfF1c-2BY81wGplvLBuYwQp-2By4y2xHmhlDkmTIh7-2FGQMldqW7a82aCTvYLLvnghXCSFbLz2152vLws6nla2TmCNDmLoTim-2Fdq9Cn40uXY24HHyxnHdfoASrcBCdGq1NoNjXJagZOc6FvPeVVYupD-2F0CvQy6Dbsjvg-2BC648RoAYHPFO9j-2FbYpcofO7LquOlKjkAw1sCLE8FGmV37xdopnN5lWDoqhCIenuWsRG-2BhlhMBRGy-2FHjg9nVm4zS6kspT-2FnWy0Jb8p97b8aM8LOcf9oZpNMaPTO6t4hrNYYOHuBqfIy4v9GtjM5cWd8HZX7MaPKp9O9cmgG7bHjM52qE6VV0FNomnEdu0QFLgE6uIVtMs2F4ml5SYYuTRIaXkEgWY8IY-2Fv-2FJ1zoTJWVyB730-3D),

security to those who work hard and strive to get ahead, according to a

A separate survey, conducted in conjunction with the nation’s 250th birthday
by AP-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research, found that half of respondents
[lost
faith](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BLD1FpQskG5FALiJlF7n4JTdntlTPa3kZHgwGRW6DWJYkGmQ-2FzeuCj6aEK1bglLUqg-3D-3DffsH_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Btfc4jeVCORt8ioA1M5PxwjGrtjF6IXFwVnowFH8MFIxJx-2Bz2FT4p75MittqFQqF4xToieODwbyqLb-2BSob5ztnoFqMsaNloKNKn4m54N2x7ZetfjDBEv7m9xHbs7wvEmhHiTZeL-2FS108x-2FKkP4d-2FiMo-2FY5Fo-2FpAF-2BNwNv6aTupu04Y34RgDHHcO88Vdzqc9rfr3cq3ZrgPCCuXCEBEzUS-2BOGMugzBxutgOkIxuPN-2BZ88qL1OLkevgz7HxUNlXwL8dHIJzkOA8g9fvK-2Bcy3Z-2FMu57-2FN-2ByvjrAXhFB6fL3iQ0Cw-2Bm6211A-2FUKOlEbkWTzEpQ8pfUYvZ-2F2CEPIiz3VASBMSpfy6QNfF1c-2BY81wGplvLBuYwQp-2By4y2xHmhlDkmTIh7-2FGQMldqW7a82aCTvYLLvnghXCSFbLz2152vLws6nla2TmCNDmLoTim-2Fdq9Cn40uXY24HHyxnHdfoASrcBCdGq1NoNjXJagZOc6FvPeVVYupD-2F0CvQy6Dbsjvg-2BC648RoAYHPFO9j-2FbYpcofO7LqugkeHS2tqxo1eIrcPizRW8FBAAMvrsLr2DQzws3RzulAc9nvIIg5z4L14Nn6QtMMDsjPD9XMjn6D5FEUPbpjXCNpyRx-2BDaomyKtM-2B8EIJ6oA5e4cavtv-2BHdg4yTX7T6zdEa9Ed-2BDn9x0d9s-2FUwnLEzg-2FeQmwe4kdYvkzmbd1iXPtJ7Lhk6fT3ae3Nmgo0ufOL17yyDyQAm1T0OxmoDIi8w-3D)

like them.

But Marcelo, president of United Steelworkers (USW) Local 12000 and a mechanic
at Southern Connecticut Gas, will be the first to say it doesn’t have to be
this way. After helping him fulfill the American dream, the union now enables
him to hold on to it.

A USW contract provides Marcelo with the good wages he needs to ride out
Donald Trump’s
[inflationary](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BKXLZB-2BN-2Bk9tuTuJ6Ge1N7nL-2BXu6EG0jEHt2S1LibkQjpRnAhyW7DNP2QSH8qqZnGEJ4-2BEYQB4YrcdR2nc0rAj-2BSw3y-2Fcbyv-2BsmR8vvufTU4MC92_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Btfc4jeVCORt8ioA1M5PxwjGrtjF6IXFwVnowFH8MFIxJx-2Bz2FT4p75MittqFQqF4xToieODwbyqLb-2BSob5ztnoFqMsaNloKNKn4m54N2x7ZetfjDBEv7m9xHbs7wvEmhHiTZeL-2FS108x-2FKkP4d-2FiMo-2FY5Fo-2FpAF-2BNwNv6aTupu04Y34RgDHHcO88Vdzqc9rfr3cq3ZrgPCCuXCEBEzUS-2BOGMugzBxutgOkIxuPN-2BZ88qL1OLkevgz7HxUNlXwL8dHIJzkOA8g9fvK-2Bcy3Z-2FMu57-2FN-2ByvjrAXhFB6fL3iQ0Cw-2Bm6211A-2FUKOlEbkWTzEpQ8pfUYvZ-2F2CEPIiz3VASBMSpfy6QNfF1c-2BY81wGplvLBuYwQp-2By4y2xHmhlDkmTIh7-2FGQMldqW7a82aCTvYLLvnghXCSFbLz2152vLws6nla2TmCNDmLoTim-2Fdq9Cn40uXY24HHyxnHdfoASrcBCdGq1NoNjXJagZOc6FvPeVVYupD-2F0CvQy6Dbsjvg-2BC648RoAYHPFO9j-2FbYpcofO7LquVQwHxLoTT2orzp08fzOSQFVARBAjW3zbhgQp-2FX3uNQ6MpjApqXx9M34HCNGwjJMvGlVOhnE2xbsPz-2F0g3hoAe6gU1wM-2FlMWzsewRAArKEcnV1OMhtOkV5yE4BhGOhTXxo4Dfs7iBQy71by9fAeUFAIUGHGSo0sWR2lkptgtzpcdWQq5l9es1zxWQdFEXfoGUm86vp5EXnlSodrbgN7ra0-3D)

The contract delivers quality, employer-sponsored health care, while more and
more Americans today have no choice but to [put off doctor’s
visits](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BBFHP8PTEtXQ4u-2BUH5Sgy284fx-2FIkjvO37sqBlUeiJmQB9-2Bd-2B38fFO-2FKcMw394uvNhiT7IRchInMJ-2BsKgRsJw9jqyKGBXqkcOwzMSV-2BGBhGTOxIT_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Btfc4jeVCORt8ioA1M5PxwjGrtjF6IXFwVnowFH8MFIxJx-2Bz2FT4p75MittqFQqF4xToieODwbyqLb-2BSob5ztnoFqMsaNloKNKn4m54N2x7ZetfjDBEv7m9xHbs7wvEmhHiTZeL-2FS108x-2FKkP4d-2FiMo-2FY5Fo-2FpAF-2BNwNv6aTupu04Y34RgDHHcO88Vdzqc9rfr3cq3ZrgPCCuXCEBEzUS-2BOGMugzBxutgOkIxuPN-2BZ88qL1OLkevgz7HxUNlXwL8dHIJzkOA8g9fvK-2Bcy3Z-2FMu57-2FN-2ByvjrAXhFB6fL3iQ0Cw-2Bm6211A-2FUKOlEbkWTzEpQ8pfUYvZ-2F2CEPIiz3VASBMSpfy6QNfF1c-2BY81wGplvLBuYwQp-2By4y2xHmhlDkmTIh7-2FGQMldqW7a82aCTvYLLvnghXCSFbLz2152vLws6nla2TmCNDmLoTim-2Fdq9Cn40uXY24HHyxnHdfoASrcBCdGq1NoNjXJagZOc6FvPeVVYupD-2F0CvQy6Dbsjvg-2BC648RoAYHPFO9j-2FbYpcofO7LqrukHiXKoQ-2F1tU3e-2BGgXC8YzR6pAcVebnD1nskJlBjDIzoxvxgkVYI9IsUcNtkvgZPdaANdPtJqEN0Sick0-2B1rYxS-2B1scMrI6AvEeDODdrFMCBhQQ-2BkmO4rH9z4-2FiZQhvZzJkAoJk0lMZQWxrzQd-2BU0KekKAU6MlCW21wijIUInynGw2TWYRjdIr0Qtx-2Bn3RZpfTMRy9tk3JSGQVG2Ar6PU-3D)
or treatments because of the spiraling costs.

“There’s the stability of knowing you have benefits,” Marcelo said of the
contract, which he and his coworkers negotiated. “You don’t have to worry.”

This is all fabulous. But it isn’t unique.

Union members across the country make [significantly more
